subject: Cognitive Science
title: Concepts in AI
description: A short lesson to help you apply Concepts in AI.

hook.text: A neural network labels a photo "husky" because of snow in the background, not the dog's features.

buildup.text: Machines learn categories from statistical patterns in data, without understanding what things are.

discovery.text: Human concepts carry causal knowledge—machines just have correlations with no explanatory depth.

twist.text: Yet large language models now pass tests of analogy and abstraction that once seemed human-only.

climax.text: Whether AI has true concepts or just convincing imitations remains cognitive science's hottest debate.

punchline.text: Machines classify, but do they understand?

quiz.question: How do AI categories differ from human categories?
options: AI relies on correlations; humans use causal understanding
